name: Altstadt Hall in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: The historic Old Town of Hall in Tirol is Western Austria's largest preserved medieval town center, famed for Hasegg Castle, the Mint Tower, and cobbled alleys.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The enchanting Historic Old Town of Hall in Tirol, situated along the Inn River just ten kilometres east of Innsbruck, stands as the largest and most pristine medieval urban ensemble in Western Austria. Enriched by lucrative salt mining in the Halltal Valley and the establishment of the sovereign mint, Hall blossomed in the late Middle Ages into an affluent trading hub that eclipsed Innsbruck in wealth and prestige. Its pedestrianized historic core captivates with narrow cobblestone alleys, romantic squares, painted Gothic townhouses, and pastel oriel windows. The undisputed architectural icon is Hasegg Castle with its twelve-sided Mint Tower: here in 1486, the sovereign struck the world's first large silver coin—the Guldiner—which gave birth to the thaler and ultimately the modern dollar. Today, Hall unites vibrant boutique shopping, university life, and cultural institutions within an authentic historical atmosphere.

Route & Anforderungen

Exploring Hall's historical center is independent of the weather, leisurely, and deeply rewarding for culture enthusiasts, couples, and families. A self-guided heritage trail links the Upper Town Square (Oberer Stadtplatz) with the late Gothic Town Hall and the imposing St. Nicholas Parish Church, descending through picturesque lanes like Schlossergasse and Rosengasse to Hasegg Castle and the Mint Museum. A complete walking tour occupies between one and a half and two and a half hours. Because the historic laneways feature authentic antique cobblestones, flat and comfortable walking shoes are strongly recommended. While level thoroughfares allow access for strollers and wheelchairs, visitors should anticipate uneven paving throughout the core.

Besuch & Anreise

Hall in Tirol is ideally situated on motorway A12 (exit Hall Mitte) and federal road B171. Ample secure underground parking is provided immediately at the edge of the historic quarter in the Altstadtgarage and Untere Stadt car parks. By train, Austrian Federal Railways (ÖBB) S-Bahn trains connect Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof to Hall in Tirol station every ten to fifteen minutes. In addition, municipal express bus 504 operates frequent departures from central Innsbruck straight to Hall's Lower Town Square.

Tipps

Climb the 186 steps of the Mint Tower at Hasegg Castle for sweeping vistas over terracotta tiled roofs towards the limestone peaks of the Karwendel mountains. Inside the Hall Mint Museum, visitors can experience the thundering drop-hammer press and strike their very own commemorative silver coin.
preis: Old town freely accessible; Hasegg Castle and Mint Tower museum apply admission
oeffnungszeiten: Old town open year-round; Mint Museum open year-round
